notes.note: #2947 (guardian allow answers plain calls only; stacked on #3100). Rewrote the opening delivery paragraph: added the guardian paragraph (what the guardian is shown per buildGuardianPrompt: agent, tool name, description, arguments; hook states no opinion; allow kept by tool-use id, used once, plain calls only, 256 bound, deny still a PreToolUse deny) and the ACP sentence (no evaluator allow answers a needs-person request). Checked each statement against claude-adapter.ts canUseTool/evaluateClaudePreToolPolicy, acp-adapter.ts requestPermission and the new adapter tests. The hook-allow recheck list (deny rules, ask rules, user-interaction tools, safety checks, MCP ceiling, sandbox override) was re-read in the bundled 2.1.278 binary's post-hook recheck function; stated as read, not live.

#2947 (guardian allow answers plain calls only; stacked on #3100). Added a paragraph under What autoApprove never covers: a guardian allow has the same limits on Claude Code and ACP, a deny in enforce mode still blocks, a denyApprovals child is denied an escalation at once, and a headless run now waits on an escalation it used to run on the guardian's allow. Checked against the adapter tests for each case. The Tool Approval Flow and Unattended runs sections describe Station's engine, where the guardian's allow is unchanged; re-read and left as written.

#2947 (guardian allow answers plain calls only; stacked on #3100). Added a paragraph to respondToRequest: a guardian allow answers a plain Claude call with no request.opened, and an escalation, plan exit or question opens a request; on ACP it answers no plan exit, question or network-host ask. Checked against canUseTool and requestPermission. The acceptForSession and structured-reason text is unaffected.

#2947 (guardian allow answers plain calls only; stacked on #3100). Rest of the guide (transport, sessions, file-system and terminal callbacks) makes no claim about the changed condition.
